title: The art of calligraphy
hookLine: writing Allah's words beautifully became the highest art

lines: A REED, A KNIFE, A SLANTED CUT.
A LONG PAUSE, THEN ONE STROKE.
cards: A reed, dried and hard, about the length of a hand. A small knife. The calligrapher holds the reed against a block of bone, cuts the tip at a slant, then splits it with one careful stroke.
The ink is dark and thick. The paper has been polished smooth. Before the first letter, a long pause.
Then the reed moves, and a single line swells and thins like a breath. A new stretch of the path begins here, the arts, and it begins with a line. Today's word: khatt.

teach.h: KHATT: A LINE, A HAND, AN ART.
teach.b: Khatt is Arabic for a line, and for handwriting, and so for the art of beautiful writing: calligraphy. Why did writing, of all things, become so central to Islamic art? Start with the Qur'an.
Muslims believe it is the speech of God, revealed in Arabic.

teach.h: BY THE PEN AND WHAT THEY WRITE.
teach.b: One surah opens with an oath on the pen itself: "Nun. By the pen and that which they write." A scripture that swears by the pen gives the pen weight.
So copying the Qur'an became an act of devotion, and doing it beautifully a way of honoring the words. Calligraphers trained for years under a master.

teach.h: LETTERS MEASURED IN DOTS, A MASTER'S LICENSE.
teach.b: Letters were measured in dots made by the tip of the pen, so every alif and every curve kept its proportion. When a student was ready, the master gave a written license, an ijaza, to sign their own work.
It names the teacher, and often the teacher's teacher, so each new calligrapher stands in a chain of hands. In the tradition's own telling, calligraphy came to stand above the other arts.
Stand before a mosque wall and you can see why: the words are the decoration. Not a picture of something holy. The holy words themselves, made beautiful.

how: Muslim calligraphers train under a master, write with a cut reed pen, and receive an ijaza when ready; their work fills mosque walls, Qur'an pages and framed panels in Muslim homes.

games.q: you've trained for years under a master calligrapher. your letters finally keep their proportions. what do you need before signing your own work?
o: an ijaza, a written license from your master.
games.why: the master gave a written license, an ijaza, to a student who was ready to sign their own work.

practice: Take a pen and any scrap of paper, and write bismillah, "In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful," in Arabic if you know it, in English, or just the one word.
Go slower than feels normal, one stroke to one breath, then write it once more without judging the first. If you are Muslim, you may say it as you write.
